subject: psychiatry
title: Psychological theories and defence mechanisms

steps.tx: Sigmund Freud founded **psychoanalysis**, a psychotherapy that analyses the mind. He proposed the structural model of mind with three parts. The **id** holds instinctual drives, works on the pleasure principle, and is present from birth. The **ego** works on the reality principle and mediates between id and outside world. The **superego** holds internalised moral standards and works on idealism, forming the conscience and ego ideal.
steps.say: Sigmund Freud founded psychoanalysis, a psychotherapy that analyses the mind. He proposed the structural model with three parts. The id holds instinctual drives, follows the pleasure principle, and is present from birth. The ego follows the reality principle and mediates between the id and the outside world. The superego holds internalised moral standards, forming the conscience and the ego ideal.

steps.tx: Freud described a **topographical** model of mind with conscious, preconscious and unconscious levels. Later he moved to the structural model. Free association, where the patient speaks whatever comes to mind on a couch, was his main method. Dreams were called the royal road to the unconscious. Freud described five psychosexual stages: oral, anal, phallic, latency and genital.

steps.tx: Defence mechanisms are unconscious ways the ego protects against anxiety. **Repression** is the basic mechanism underlying all others, and is involuntary. **Suppression** is a conscious, voluntary postponement of an impulse and is a mature mechanism. Mature mechanisms include sublimation, altruism, humour, suppression and anticipation. Immature ones include acting out, regression and projection. Sublimation redirects an unacceptable drive into a socially valued activity.

steps.tx: Erik Erikson described eight **psychosocial** stages, each with a crisis to resolve. Infancy is trust versus mistrust. Early childhood is autonomy versus shame. Adolescence is identity versus role confusion. Jean Piaget described cognitive stages, from sensorimotor to formal operations. Ivan Pavlov's classical conditioning pairs a neutral stimulus with an unconditioned one. B F Skinner's operant conditioning uses reinforcement and punishment. Positive reinforcement adds a reward, negative reinforcement removes an aversive stimulus, and extinction removes a reward.

right.title: Conditioning and attachment
points: Attachment theory: bond with caregiver shapes later relationships

steps.tx: Attachment theory, developed by John Bowlby, proposes that an infant's early **bond** with a primary caregiver forms an **internal working model** that shapes later relationships. Mary Ainsworth's Strange Situation identified secure and insecure patterns. Donald Winnicott described **transitional objects**, such as a soft blanket, which comfort a child when the mother is absent. These objects typically appear around six months of age, bridging dependence and independence.
